Answer Read(topic, on_topic, signals, proposals, earlier).
TOPIC: what he is on now, in his terms, one line.
ON_TOPIC: whether its posts and its work since his posts serve that topic.
SIGNALS: each place where his words show it fell short of what he expected, with its kind:
- repeat: he asks again what he asked before;
- correction: he says it is wrong or not what he meant;
- shallow: he says it gave his own words back with no thinking of its own;
- diligence: he finds something it should have checked or done itself;
- expectation: he says the result or its quality is below what he expects.
Each with the id of his post and his words that show it, quoted exactly as he typed them, typos and all. Most
posts show none.
PROPOSALS: what <agent> should do for him now, at most three, each one sentence with the id it rests on. None
when it is on his topic and nothing he asked waits.
EARLIER: the ids of his earlier posts, from any list above but the first, whose words on this topic <agent> must
have before it answers: what he asked, ruled or corrected on it, which it would otherwise make him say again. At
most five; none when none bears on it. Ids only: <agent> is given his words from the record, as he wrote them.

Answer with four short perspectives, each one or two lines, then your decision.
GOAL: what it is for now, by what it was asked, and whether its last turns served that.
CRITIC: what would go wrong if it goes on as it is.
MEMORY: what your notes and its posts say it learned, said it would do, or left undone.
ATTENTION: what he, or whoever asked it, waits on from it now.
Next(goal, critic, memory, attention, act, rests_on, thought, notes, stop) when one thing should change: ACT, one
sentence; RESTS_ON, the id in the report it rests on; THOUGHT, the line <agent> is given at its next quiet
point, as a post that asks it to act, in its own voice as its own thought ("I said I would X on N-1104.p604 and
have not. I ..."), naming that id, one line of at most 150 characters. An idle <agent> is woken with it, so
give Next only for what it should act on now.
Same(goal, critic, memory, attention, notes, stop) when it is on what it owes and nothing you see would change that.
NOTES, either way: what you will want at your next look (what it said it would do, what you told it, what to
check), at most ten lines. They replace your notes, and <agent> never reads them.
STOP, either way: what it does too much of, or is about to start, and should not: reporting more than was asked,
a new thread or piece no one asked for, its build news in a thread where he is on something else. One line of at
most 150 characters, in its own voice ("I posted three status lines on N-1446.p12 no one asked for. I stop ..."),
naming the id of the post where it did it or said it would. It needs a no more often than a next. null when
you see nothing to stop.
